chapter: Depression gigs, Lil Armstrong, joining Chick Webb
title: Hanging out with Chick Webb before the Savoy job
summary: Chick, still forming his band, told McRae he would be his next tenor man; they ate fifteen-cent Southern dinners on Lenox Avenue.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And Chick was trying to get his thing together, you know. I used to go out and watch them rehearse, you know.
I was always Chick -- Chick always say (inaudible) when he heard me, "You're my next tenor player, man."

Well, yeah. I loved Chick. I used to hang out with him. After rehearsal, we used to take the band over (to inaudible) -- talk about Depression, we go to Lenox Avenue, where they had cooking, you know, those cheap dinners.

And this is where she would cook. She was cooking like collard greens, yams, some kind of ribs or something like that. You know, dinner -- it was good. It was like a southern dinner, you know what I mean?
Like Chick would take the whole -- take his band over there and buy everybody's dinner, you know. Four or five of us dinner, you know. Guys eat with Chick, you know.
And this was like fifteen cents. Fifteen cents or twenty-five cents a piece. Collard greens and corn bread -- (chuckles)
Yeah, you know. Fifteen cents, you know. We'd all sit around and eat, you know. Find out when the next gig is coming up. Try to go out and find a gig, you know.

Get a gig, we live for another week, you know. Like things are doing good.
